platform.windows: compiles; the Windows session path is T6 and no Windows peer run has been recorded

upstream.role: the peer is a Mihomo `listeners:` endpoint; the Rust kernel is the client and a controlled loopback sink (TCP) or loopback UDP echo records what arrived

wrapper: tool/kernel-compat/peer-tests.sh (resolves the repository root, the cache and the pinned binary; cargo test runs from native-kernel/crates/billow-kernel, so a relative KC_MIHOMO_BIN does not resolve)

socks5.notes: the peer replies success after its SOCKS5 handshake but before dialing, so the positive case is judged by the tagged bytes the sink received; UDP is not part of this family (udp: true is rejected)

http.notes: Mihomo's HTTP inbound writes 200 before dialing, so only the receiving side proves a positive tunnel; a wrong credential is answered with 407 and the kernel reports 502

ss.peer: listeners: type: shadowsocks, aes-256-gcm (the listener serves TCP and UDP)
ss.notes: TCP uses the AEAD-2017 stream framing and both directions; UDP uses one AEAD datagram per packet with the peer's own salt. The UDP peer's ruleset forwards DIRECT to the loopback UDP echo because the sink is a TCP proxy. The loopback peer test `shadowsocks_udp_datagrams_are_forwarded_with_the_peers_aead` covers aes-256-gcm with an independent decoder; `shadowsocks_aes_256_gcm_roundtrip` / `..._chacha20_ietf_poly1305_roundtrip` cover the other ciphers over TCP. A `udp: true` proxy with `dialer-proxy` sends its datagrams through the hop's SOCKS5 UDP relay (Mihomo's global `socks-port` serves UDP); the peer case with `MATCH,REJECT` at the hop proves the chain is used, because a direct association would have reached the echo.

trojan.peer: listeners: type: trojan with a self-signed certificate
trojan.notes: wrong password and an untrusted certificate are both checked for TCP; UDP opens command 3 and exchanges `addr|length|CRLF|payload` frames, a wrong password ends the stream and the echo stays untouched A `udp: true` trojan with `dialer-proxy` opens its server connection through the hop's TCP CONNECT (like the TCP path) and rides the UDP frames on it; the peer case with `MATCH,REJECT` at the hop proves the chain, because a direct stream would have reached the echo.

vless.notes: the ws cases record the two pinned handshakes: a standard upgrade (no `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, which Mihomo reads as 0-RTT early data) and the key-less v2ray HTTP upgrade that turns the stream raw; the Host override only changes the upgrade request

anytls.notes: one stream per connection, protocol version 2; the server's SYNACK is not awaited before the payload is sent, as sing's client does; UDP needs UoT and is rejected

dialer-proxy.peer: two Mihomo listeners (mixed as the exit hop, socks as the first hop)
dialer-proxy.notes: only a socks5 hop can carry another hop; a closed first hop fails the dial instead of falling back to DIRECT, and other chains are rejected at load time or with a chain error. UDP follows the same chain (see ss and loopbackOnlyEvidence.chained_udp_positive).

vmess.peer: listeners: type: vmess with one `users: [{uuid, alterId: 0}]` entry (sing-vmess server)
vmess.notes: The Rust client sends the AEAD request header and the record layer; the peer's `MATCH,sink-http` rule forwards to the controlled sink. `auto` resolves to aes-128-gcm on this host, `chacha20-poly1305` is exercised explicitly, the domain case sends `localhost` as a domain address so the peer resolves it, and the websocket case uses the peer's `ws-path` over TLS. A wrong uuid is rejected by the peer's auth id check, so the sink is never reached. UDP, the legacy alterId header and the non-tcp/ws transports are rejected at load time.

snell.peer: listeners: type: snell with `psk`, `version: 1|2|3` (and `obfs-opts: {mode: http, host: bing.com}` for v3)
snell.notes: v1 is chacha20-poly1305 and v2/v3 aes-128-gcm over the Argon2id-derived record layer; the v3 case adds the simple-obfs HTTP layer. A wrong psk fails the record authentication, so the sink is never reached. v4-v6, `reuse`, `mode` and the obfs `tls` mode are rejected at load time.

trusttunnel.notes: The Rust client opens TLS with ALPN h2, sends CONNECT with `Proxy-Authorization: Basic` and carries the tunnel in DATA frames; the peer forwards to the controlled sink. A wrong password is answered with 407 before any stream exists, so the sink is never reached. UDP (`_udp2`), ICMP (`_icmp`), QUIC and the pooled multiplexing options are rejected at load time.

gost-relay.peer: controlled gost relay v2 server in tests/protocols.rs, written from transport/gost/relay.go: request/response header, auth, address and network features, the UDP association (`length(u16 BE) || payload`) and a version-1 smux session (SYN/PSH/FIN frames); `tool/kernel-compat/peers/gost-relay-harness` is the pinned `gost.NewRelayDialer` (mux + UDP) driving the same peer, so the server framing is checked against the locked dialer as well as against our client
gost-relay.notes: the UDP association is bound to one target like relayPacketConn, so a new destination replaces it; a server that refuses the UDP command produces no reply and the kernel never falls back to DIRECT. The smux session is the pinned `DefaultConfig` version 1 with keep-alive disabled, one stream per dial. The pinned-dialer harness is run by tool/kernel-compat/family-peers.sh; the CLI process cases cover a plain TCP relay and the `mux` session (`cli_process_tunnels_through_gost_relay_mux`).

ssh.peer: controlled SSH server built on russh in tests/protocols.rs: password and public-key auth, host-key pinning, one direct-tcpip channel per dial to a loopback echo target
ssh.notes: The pinned Mihomo has no SSH listener. The peer enforces the SSH protocol independently of the outbound; the client is tested with password auth, Ed25519 public-key auth and a pinned host key (match and mismatch). A private-key file path is rejected at load time (inline PEM only).

ssr.peer: two independent Go peers. `peers/ssr-server` (origin/plain, built on the pinned shadowstream package) and `peers/ssr-plugins`, the server side of every pinned protocol and obfs plugin plus the UDP association, written from the pinned client code with the roles swapped. `peers/ssr-plugins -client` runs the *pinned* obfs/protocol packages as a client, and family-peers.sh requires it to accept the peer for all 36 protocol/obfs combinations before the Rust matrix runs.
ssr.notes: the plugin matrix covers all 6 protocols x 6 obfs; the wrong-password cases run for every auth plugin with plain and tls1.2_ticket_auth; the protocol-param case exercises the user id/key path with payloads larger than the 8100/2800-byte record split; UDP has no obfs layer in the pinned outbound and is verified for every protocol. The Go peer derives the server framing from the pinned client code (the locked tree has no SSR listener) and documents the two pinned quirks it mirrors: the client discards two bytes of the server's first auth_chain record, and the auth_chain UDP reply hashes auth+uid while the request hashes auth only. The random_head head boundary is found by scanning the CRC from the longest candidate: the pinned check also matches one byte short for some lengths, which produced an intermittent `auth_* wrong mac` in the controlled runs before the scan order was fixed. The CLI process case `cli_process_tunnels_through_an_ssr_plugin` drives an `auth_chain_b` + `tls1.2_ticket_auth` tunnel through the real binary (controlled entry only). The peer's address read and the client roundtrips are bounded so a wrong password fails in seconds instead of hanging. Residual ambiguity: the pinned random_head format carries no explicit length, so a TCP split exactly one byte before the head end on a length that admits the short boundary could still mis-slice; it did not reproduce in 300 controlled connections or in 10 repeated matrix runs after the scan order was fixed.

tuic.peer: listeners: type: tuic, users: {uuid: password}, certificate/private-key (UDP-only QUIC listener)
tuic.notes: TUIC v5: one unidirectional auth stream with the TLS-exporter token, one bidirectional Connect stream per TCP target. The wrong-password case closes the QUIC connection with AuthenticationFailed before any stream reaches the sink. UDP relay modes are not implemented and are recorded in rust-mapping.json.

hysteria2.peer: listeners: type: hysteria2, users: {name: password}, certificate/private-key (UDP-only QUIC listener)
hysteria2.notes: Hysteria2: HTTP/3 POST /auth (status 233) followed by a 0x401 TCP request frame on a bidirectional stream. The Rust client implements the minimal HTTP/3/QPACK subset the auth exchange needs (static table + Huffman, no dynamic table). A wrong password is a non-233 status and is reported as a 502 before the tunnel reply.

hysteria.peer: controlled quinn server implementing transport/hysteria/core/protocol.go (control hello + per-session request/response)
hysteria.notes: Hysteria v1 has no Mihomo listener in the pinned v1.19.34 tree (only hysteria2/tuic/shadowquic listeners), so the recipe's locked-Mihomo-peer requirement cannot be met for this family. The peer is a controlled quinn server written from the pinned transport/hysteria/core/protocol.go (ClientHello/ServerHello and per-session request/response); TCP, auth-str and base64 auth are covered, while port hopping/XPlus/faketcp/wechat/UDP are rejected by name. This is recorded as a T10 gap in t10-feasibility.json (hysteriaPeerGap), not a pass against Mihomo.

mieru.peer: listeners: type: mieru (transport: TCP, users: {alice: "..."}); the peer runs the GPL-3.0 enfein/mieru v3.39.0 server module inside the pinned binary
mieru.notes: the kernel's mieru client is an independent implementation of the published TCP protocol (no mieru code vendored or linked). A wrong password is answered with silence (the peer drains the connection for up to a minute), so the client bounds the wait for the session reply and the kernel reports 502. TCP sessions only: `transport: UDP`, `udp: true`, mieru multiplexing and traffic-pattern are rejected at load with the reason recorded.

shadowquic.peer: listeners: type: shadowquic with a `users: [{username, password}]` account and a loopback UDP `jls-upstream` camouflage socket; the peer runs the pinned jls-tls/jls-quic-go listener
shadowquic.notes: the JLS ClientHello/ServerHello `random` seal is an independent Rust implementation of the locked jls-tls algorithm (`src/outbound/jls.rs`), cross-checked against real messages emitted by the pinned Go package in `tool/kernel-compat/peers/shadowquic-jls-vectors` (vectors committed at `native-kernel/crates/billow-kernel/tests/data/shadowquic-jls.txt`). The QUIC transport is quinn 0.11; the custom ClientHello random is injected by a recorded-random replay of rustls's own ClientHello, and the replay is checked byte-for-byte before the connection proceeds. UDP is covered in both pinned carriers (QUIC datagrams and `udp-over-stream`). A datagram payload is bounded by the path MTU as well as `max-datagram-frame-size` (quinn starts at 1200 bytes); a larger payload fails with a named error and `udp-over-stream` carries large packets as u16-length frames. A wrong password is forwarded to the camouflage upstream and the client aborts before sending a request; the kernel reports 502. `zero-rtt`, QUIC `v2`, `congestion-controller`, `bbr-profile`, a non-default `cwnd`, `up`/`down` (Brutal) and `dialer-proxy` are rejected at load with the reason recorded. The BasicOption knobs (tfo/mptcp/interface-name/routing-mark/ip-version) are rejected when enabled and accepted as no-ops; the option matrix covers both forms.

masque.peer: two controlled HTTP/3 peers in tests/quic_peers.rs (quinn servers, ALPN h3, their own QPACK/capsule codecs): a CONNECT-UDP peer with SETTINGS_ENABLE_CONNECT_PROTOCOL, and a CONNECT-IP peer that requires the WARP client certificate, advertises SETTINGS_H3_DATAGRAM 0x33 and draft-00 0x276, answers `cf-connect-ip`, reads ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT, assigns 172.16.0.2/32 and fd00::2/128, and echoes tunnelled IPv4/IPv6 UDP packets with its own independent IP/UDP codec; no pinned listener
masque.notes: T18 implements the pinned Cloudflare WARP CONNECT-IP shape (RFC 9484) and keeps T14's RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP subset. The pinned `adapter/outbound/masque.go` has no `listeners:` mode and a WARP registration endpoint is not reachable offline, so no pinned-binary interop is claimed: the CONNECT-IP peer is a controlled HTTP/3 server. The positive cases check the request (:method CONNECT, :protocol cf-connect-ip, authority/path from the default uri, capsule-protocol ?1), the ROUTE_ADVERTISEMENT capsule, ADDRESS_ASSIGN, a self-signed client certificate carrying the configured P-256 key (the peer verifies it is required and records its SPKI), endpoint-key pinning (a wrong pin fails), IPv4 and IPv6 UDP echo paths (the peer validates both checksums), and DNS resolution through the tunnel (a hostname target becomes an A query carried as a tunnelled IP/UDP packet). The negative cases cover a peer without HTTP Datagrams, ADDRESS_REQUEST, a 403, a peer without extended CONNECT, a 200 without the capsule protocol, an untrusted certificate, and the named refusal of TCP (no TCP state machine). The CLI paths are cli.rs::process_loads_t18_masque_connect_ip and family_cli.rs::cli_process_tunnels_udp_through_masque_connect_ip.

sudoku.peer: listeners: type: sudoku with the default (entropy table, pure downlink, legacy HTTP mask) and the configured variants (prefer_ascii, up_ascii_down_entropy, custom-table(s), enable-pure-downlink: false, disable-http-mask, aead-method)
sudoku.notes: GPL-3.0-derived translation of the pinned `transport/sudoku` (T17; see t17 below). Table construction uses Go's math/rand shuffle, so the 288-grid order matches; both pure and packed downlink codecs, the record layer (chacha20poly1305/aes-128-gcm/none), the KIP X25519/HKDF handshake, the session mux (two streams, sequential and concurrent) and a `dialer-proxy` chain (a recording SOCKS5 hop carries the exit's server connection; T17-A3) are covered. `tool/kernel-compat/peers/sudoku-vectors` is the locked Go codec used by `tests/protocols.rs::sudoku_codec_matches_the_pinned_implementation` (pinned encode -> Rust decode, Rust encode -> pinned decode, with and without padding) for entropy/ascii/directional/custom tables. HTTP tunnel modes and UoT are rejected at load with the reason recorded.

easytier.command: KC_EASYTIER_PEER_BIN=... cargo test --manifest-path native-kernel/Cargo.toml --locked --test mesh_peers easytier_pinned_core_cleartext -- --ignored --test-threads=1
easytier.peer: tool/kernel-compat/peers/easytier-peer (locked easytier-go wasm core, enable_encryption=false, no secure mode)

negative: wrong network secret is rejected (cleartext and secure)

easytier.notes: T20 LGPL-3.0-or-later translation of the cleartext, Noise XX and secure-datagram/AES-GCM/ChaCha20 path; OSPF/route and device/TUN remain T6/T7. See evidence/t20-easytier.md.

loopbackOnlyEvidence.custom_tls_roots: tests/protocols.rs::custom_ca_roots_are_installed_for_outbound_tls starts a private CA and a server certificate it signs, then runs trojan, vless and socks5-tls with and without `tls: {custom-cert: [<ca>]}`: without the anchor every handshake fails, with it every tunnel reaches the echo. It is loopback because the peer needs a certificate this test controls.
loopbackOnlyEvidence.udp_direct_and_reject: tests/protocols.rs::socks5_udp_associate_forwards_datagrams_and_honours_reject covers the inbound relay, DIRECT forwarding and a REJECT rule without an external process.
loopbackOnlyEvidence.chained_udp_positive: tests/protocols.rs::shadowsocks_udp_goes_through_the_dialer_proxy_hop uses two controlled hops (a SOCKS5 UDP server that relays, and an independent ss UDP server) and asserts the hop saw the association and relayed to the ss server. A positive chained case against Mihomo on loopback is not possible: its own loopback detector refuses to forward a datagram that came from its socks UDP listener to a local destination, so the peer case is the rejecting one.
loopbackOnlyEvidence.trojan_udp_reconnect: tests/protocols.rs::trojan_udp_reconnects_after_the_server_closes_the_stream proves that a server-closed UDP stream is retired and re-established on the next datagram of the same association.
loopbackOnlyEvidence.chained_trojan_udp_positive: tests/protocols.rs::trojan_udp_goes_through_the_dialer_proxy_hop uses a controlled SOCKS5 TCP hop and a trojan UDP peer, and asserts the hop carried the server connection and the peer served the payload.
loopbackOnlyEvidence.domain_server_chained_udp: tests/protocols.rs::shadowsocks_udp_chained_with_a_domain_server_keeps_the_replies configures `server: localhost` behind a hop: the hop resolves the name and reports the IP in its reply header, so the kernel compares resolved addresses instead of the configured string.
loopbackOnlyEvidence.masque_connect_udp: tests/quic_peers.rs drives the kernel's SOCKS5 UDP association through a controlled HTTP/3 CONNECT-UDP peer (per-destination flows, refusal, missing extended CONNECT, missing capsule negotiation, untrusted certificate, TCP refusal, same-destination reopen after the peer FIN, and a 33rd destination after 32 closed flows). A Mihomo peer is impossible: the pinned masque adapter is a Cloudflare WARP CONNECT-IP client with no listener. The shipped CLI's SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE is covered by family_cli.rs::cli_process_tunnels_udp_through_masque.

notCovered: UDP for socks5, vless (packet-addr/XUDP), anytls (UoT), gost-relay and ssr: `udp: true` is rejected at load time; no UDP association exists for those families
fragmented SOCKS5 UDP datagrams (FRAG != 0) are dropped instead of reassembled
separate `listeners:` entries on the Rust side (T5); the peer side uses them because the peer is Mihomo
platforms other than macOS arm64; DNS answers, rule families beyond the implemented list, TUN/system-proxy takeover (T6)
a positive chained UDP case against the Mihomo peer on loopback (peer-side loopback detector); the positive path is covered by two controlled hops instead

families still unimplemented after T15 (the device families and the T5 adapters): see tool/kernel-compat/evidence/rust-mapping.json#familiesNotImplemented. masque is partial: CONNECT-UDP is covered above, CONNECT-IP/TCP is rejected by name and has no peer case. shadowquic is partial: TCP/UDP and JLS are covered above; zero-rtt and the Brutal congestion options are rejected by name.

WireGuard/OpenVPN positive data-path cases stop at the IP packet (WireGuard ICMP echo through the locked device; OpenVPN AEAD keepalive decrypt): TCP/UDP through the tunnel needs the T6/T7 userspace IP stack and TUN device.

sudoku: the T17-A1 clean-room attempt stayed blocked (the keyed table, KIP handshake and record layers are not publicly specified; evidence/t17-cleanroom.md, evidence/t17-observe.log). T17-A2 translated the pinned GPL-3.0 module (see t17): TCP sessions with the legacy HTTP mask, pure/packed downlink, three record AEAD methods, the session mux and a `dialer-proxy` chain are covered by 14 pinned-peer cases; `udp: true` (UoT) and the HTTP tunnel modes are rejected at load and have no peer case.

t9.statusAfterT16: all families resolved: mieru (T13 clean-room), sudoku (T17 GPL-3.0 translation), masque (T14 CONNECT-UDP partial), shadowquic (T15 partial), wireguard/openvpn (T16 transport partial); mesh families rejected by name

controlledPeers.note: These peers are local controlled servers, not Mihomo listeners. gost-relay and ssr have independent server-side implementations of the pinned wire formats (the SSR cipher bytes and framing are pinned by the Go server and vectors); ssh uses a real SSH server; the Sudoku section builds the locked Go codec (`peers/sudoku-vectors`, GPL-3.0 test-only) and runs the Rust-vs-Go differential. `result` counts the 15 test functions of that group (gost 5, ssh 4, ssr Rust 3 + independent Go 2, sudoku codec 1); T16's WireGuard/OpenVPN peers are recorded under `t16` and run by the same script.
controlledPeers.cli: native-kernel/crates/billow-kernel-cli/tests/family_cli.rs drives one success tunnel through the real CLI process for gost-relay, ssh and ssr.

t16.dependencyDecision: WireGuard: no wireguard/boringtun crate offline; implemented in-tree with blake2 0.10.6 (new direct dependency, already in Cargo.lock), x25519-dalek, chacha20poly1305 and rand. OpenVPN: no Rust crate offline; implemented in-tree with rustls/ring, aes-gcm, chacha20poly1305, hmac/sha1 and the small MD5 already in keys.rs. The peers are the locked MIT metacubex/wireguard-go device and the OpenVPN 2.7.9 Homebrew binary; neither is linked. No source is vendored or copied line-by-line; the pinned GPL adapters were read for functional facts (not a certified clean-room; see t16-provenance.md).
t16.deviceLayer: Both transports expose IP packets; device/TUN and the userspace IP stack are T6/T7.

license.wireguard_peer: metacubex/wireguard-go MIT, golang.org/x/crypto BSD-3-Clause; test program only.
license.openvpn_peer: OpenVPN 2.7.9 binary GPL-2.0; test process only, not linked.
license.kernel: GPL-3.0-only (workspace, because of the T17 sudoku translation); for T16 itself no GPL source is vendored, linked or translated. The pinned GPL-3.0 adapters were read for functional wire facts; provenance and the no-copy audit limits are in tool/kernel-compat/evidence/t16-provenance.md.

outOfScope.note: Moved to T19 (evidence/t19-mesh.md); T16 only covers wireguard/openvpn.

t18.note: T18 implemented CONNECT-IP (RFC 9484) with the pinned WARP configuration shape, a minimal IPv4/IPv6/UDP stack, key-derived client certificates and endpoint-key pinning, and tunnel DNS; TCP over the tunnel and the h2/h3-l4proxy modes stay rejected by name. The 16 masque cases (8 CONNECT-IP, 8 CONNECT-UDP) are in the default suite and need no external binary.
